name: Joshua, Phoenix's Dominant // Phoenix, Warden of Fire
oracle_text:
When Joshua enters, discard up to two cards, then draw that many cards.
{3}{R}{W}, {T}: Exile Joshua, then return it to the battlefield transformed under its owner's control. Activate only as a sorcery.
blocked_sentences: When Joshua enters, discard up to two cards, then draw that many cards.
{3}{R}{W}, {T}: Exile Joshua, then return it to the battlefield transformed under its owner's control. Activate only as a sorcery.

needs.what: an `up_to` (or optional-count) form of the `discard` op, letting the discarding player choose any number from zero to N -- "discard up to two cards" must be satisfiable with 0, 1 or 2 cards, chosen by the player as the effect resolves
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `op_discard` evaluates `amount` to a single number and calls `ask_objects(..., take, take, ...)` with the same value as both floor and ceiling, so the count is always exact and never declinable. The `optional` key in `selector_keys` is a *target* modifier and `discard` takes no target spec; `up_to` exists in the codebase only on `choose_mode` bounds and on `TargetSpec`, neither of which reaches a discard count

needs.what: a value leaf reading how many cards the *immediately preceding discard in this same resolution* actually put into the graveyard, so "then draw that many cards" can be written as the `amount` of a following `draw`. The `as`-binding shape `exile`, `sacrifice` and `reveal` already use (record the chosen objects, read them back with `{"count": {"binding": ...}}`) is the obvious road: give `discard` an `as` and the value follows for free
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `discard` writes no binding at all, so nothing downstream can name what it took. The nearest `value_keys` entry, `cards_to_graveyard_this_turn`, is a turn-wide integer counting every card that reached any graveyard this turn -- creatures dying, spells resolving, other discards -- so it is a different number in every game state but the empty one. `cards_in_hand` measured before and after cannot be subtracted: there is no arithmetic over two snapshots of a value, only `minus` over two leaves evaluated at the same instant

needs.what: an op that exiles a permanent and immediately returns it to the battlefield **transformed, under its owner's control** -- as a new object, so it enters, its enters triggers fire, it is summoning sick, and counters/auras/control effects on the old object are gone. The Final Fantasy "Dominant" transforming cycle prints this line on both faces
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `transform` (ops_board.py `op_transform`) turns the permanent over **in place**: it calls `primitives.transform` on the live object, so the permanent never changes zones, keeps its counters, attachments and summoning-sickness state, and fires no leaves-the-battlefield or enters triggers. That is a materially stronger and differently-timed card. `exile` can move it out but has no return path other than `until_leaves` (the O-Ring link, which hands back on a later trigger, untransformed), and neither `put_onto_battlefield` nor `return_from_graveyard` accepts any "arrives on its back face" flag -- the only back-face-on-arrival path in the engine is `graveyard_cast_transformed`, which is disturb/`stack.py` and applies to *casting* the card from the graveyard, not to an activated ability on the battlefield. `meld` is the one op that does the exile-and-re-enter dance, but it is hard-wired to `melds_with`/`melds_into` and needs a partner permanent

needs.what: the packet for a transforming double-faced card must carry the **back face's printed text**. This packet gives only the front face's `oracle_text` while `type_line` names a back face ("Legendary Enchantment Creature -- Saga Phoenix"), so the `back` half of the answer -- which the answer format does support, see `henrika_domnathi_henrika_infernal_seer.json` -- cannot be written without inventing the Saga's chapters
needs.why_existing_wont_do: `back_face` in `schema.py` requires a real second card entry in the pool, and the residual gate holds every printed line to an ability. With no back-face oracle text in the packet there is nothing to author it from, and a `transform`-family ability pointing at an absent or guessed back face is worse than no card
